news.title: Captain Mubanga leads Kanyemba’s provisional Zambia U-17 World Cup squad
news.lede: Zambia Under-17 Women’s National Team captain Taonga Mubanga leads a 35-member provisional squad named by coach Carol Kanyemba for next month’s FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. Mubanga, who was part of Zambia’s squad at the previous World Cup, is among four players with previous tournament experience included in Kanyemba’s provisional group. She is joined by fellow returning players Esther Ngabwe, Grace Phiri and Beatrice Njobvu, as Kanyemba begins the final phase of preparations for Zambia’s third consecutive appearance at the global tournament. The Copper Princesses will enter a long-haul training camp this weekend, with the programme set to culminate in a pre-tournament international camp.

news.lede: Italy is the latest to withdraw their endorsement of Infantino after his botched World Cup sell-off plan. From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. news.title: From Segura to Maltby: six breakout stars from the Women’s Under-20 World Cup
news.lede: With an incredible array of talent on show we select half a dozen players who could make the step up to the senior World Cup next year. The 2026 Under-20 Women’s World Cup is entering the knockout stage in Poland and, after an intriguing group stage, we pick some of the young stars who have stood out. Celia Segura (Spain and Barcelona) Segura is no stranger to knockout football having helped Spain to silver at the Under-17 World Cup two years ago and finishing with the Bronze Ball and Bronze Boot. She has picked up the mantleagain as La Roja eased through their group.

news.title: Spain manager Luis de la Fuente agrees contract extension until 2030 World Cup
news.lede: MADRID, Sept 15 : Spain's World Cup-winning coach Luis de la Fuente has agreed a contract extension until 2030 after guiding the men's national team to back-to-back major titles, media reported on Tuesday,. De la Fuente, who led Spain to glory at Euro 2024 before winning the World Cup in July, had a contract in place until 2028. The new deal ensures that de la Fuente will remain in charge when Spain attempt to defend their global title on home soil. Spain will co-host the 2030 World Cup with Morocco and Portugal.

news.title: UEFA pressure on Infantino grows as Greek FA, Bierhoff back change
news.lede: THESSALONIKI, Greece, Sept 15 - Greek Football Association president Makis Gagatsis and former Germany national team director Oliver Bierhoff on Tuesday backed UEFA's push for change in FIFA's leadership, underscoring a united European front in opposition to FIFA president Gianni Infantino. "The Greek FA (EPO) has taken a clear position against a candidacy of Gianni Infantino," EPO President Makis Gagatsis told reporters. "We saw things happen at the World Cup that are not acceptable to football public opinion," Gagatsis said. "Then... came a programme to sell World Cup rights and we are clearly against it, so we withdrew our support of the FIFA president."

news.title: Scotland call for Sevilla forward Robbie Ure in post-World Cup reset under new coach Pocognoli
news.lede: GLASGOW, Scotland (AP) — A transfer to Spain and change of Scotland coach finally earned Sevilla striker Robbie Ure a first international call Tuesday in a reset after a disappointing World Cup where the Tartan Army of fans far outperformed the team. Scotland’s new coach Sébastien Pocognoli made the 22-year-old Ure the standout inclusion among sweeping changes for four games in a second-tier Nations League group where World Cup quarterfinalist Switzerland starts favorite. news.title: Thomas Tuchel is still bruised and bitter over England World Cup criticism - does he have a point?
news.lede: Thomas Tuchel still feels very hard done by. In fact, it would be fair to say the England manager has been bruised by the whole World Cup 2026 experience. England finished third in the World Cup, their best-ever performance on foreign soil. So, why are so many England fans still so frustrated, still hurt and why, when looking back upon the summer, do they do it with regret rather than happy memories?

news.title: New Scotland boss calls-up just 14 World Cup players as Oli McBurnie picked for first time in nearly six years
news.lede: The Hull City striker was controversially left out of Steve Clarke's World Cup squad despite helping fire the Tigers to promotion. His omission came despite scoring 17 Championship goals as well as the winner in the play-off final last term. He has since featured in all four of Hull's Premier League outings this season. McBurnie, who has featured 17 times at senior international level, could now win his first cap since appearing against the Faroe Islands in March 2021.
